_status: STAGED 2026-08-07. Built from EU/slices/_staging batches 16-26, 30-37, 44, 45, 66. Every quote re-fetched and re-read at source this session; full record in EU/ESSQualityFramework_PartA_2026-08-07.md.
_note: The ESS's self-regulatory quality stack, which the blob had staged across twenty-two batches and no session had ever built. The Code of Practice names its own composition ('the common quality framework ... is composed of the European Statistics Code of Practice, the Quality Assurance Framework ... and the general quality management principles'), and each layer below it names the layer above in its own words, ending outside the EU entirely at the SDMX Glossary.
_headline: A five-node chain in which every link is stated by the dependent document about itself: EHQMR -> SIMS -> SDMX Glossary, with QAF -> CoP alongside, and the two existing EU governance nodes (ESGAB annual report, ESS peer review final report) attaching to the CoP. It is the EU branch's first documented chain that leaves the EU layer downward into an international standard rather than upward into a Regulation.
_open_questions: Direction is genuinely two-way between the CoP and the peer reviews and this session minted only one leg. Eurostat's own 'History of the CoP' table says each revision was 'based on the results of' a peer-review round, which would be eu-statistics-code-of-practice -> ess-peer-review-final-report. It was not minted because the quote names the results of a round, not the titled final report. Both may hold; a future session with the SWD text in hand should settle it.

ess-handbook-quality-metadata-reports -> eu-statistics-code-of-practice is recorded as 'cites' on 'It supports compliance with the European Statistics Code of Practice'. That is a purpose statement, and the choice between 'cites' and 'methodology_depends_on' is a judgement, flagged rather than resolved.
The EHQMR contradicts itself about its own edition inside one document: the cover says '2021 re-edition', the foreword says 'This 2020 edition'. Both quoted in Part A; not adjudicated.

sdmx-glossary is the corpus's first SDMX node and its cadence is the weakest of the five: the document says it is a 'living' document that 'will grow and be updated' but states no interval. releases_per_year is derived from observed versions, not from a stated commitment.

reports.title: European Statistics Code of Practice
reports.publisher: European Statistical System Committee (published by Eurostat)
reports.description: The ESS's self-regulatory quality standard, adopted by the European Statistical System Committee and applying to Eurostat and the national statistical authorities. Eurostat's own page: 'The European Statistics Code of Practice (CoP) is the cornerstone of the quality framework and sets the standards for developing, producing and disseminating European statistics. It defines 16 key principles for the institutional environment under which the EU and national statistical authorities operate, as well as for the statistical processes and output . It also includes a set of 84 indicators for the best practices and standards for each of the 16 principles.' The current edition's own title page reads 'Adopted by the European Statistical System Committee 16th November 2017'. It names its own place in a three-part framework: 'The common quality framework of the European Statistical System is composed of the European Statistics Code of Practice, the Quality Assurance Framework of the European Statistical System and the general quality management principles'.
reports.cadence_note: Revised editions, not periodic issues. Eurostat's 'History of the CoP' table gives three dated events and nothing else: '24 February 2005 Adoption of the CoP by the Statistical Programme Committee | September 2011 Revision of the CoP based on the results of the 1st round of ESS peer reviews | November 2017 Revision of the CoP based on the results of the 2nd round of ESS peer reviews'. Two revisions across twelve years is roughly one every six; 0.17 is that observed interval, not a stated commitment. Same treatment as the versioned-standard nodes (esa-2010, sna-2008).

reports.title: Quality Assurance Framework of the European Statistical System
reports.publisher: European Statistical System Committee (published by Eurostat)
reports.description: The implementation-side half of the ESS common quality framework, sitting under the Code of Practice. Eurostat's own page: 'The QAF serves as complementary guidance for how to implement the CoP. Like the CoP, it applies to the statistical authorities of the ESS, which comprises the European Union Statistical Authority (Eurostat), the National Statistical Institutes (NSIs), and Other National Authorities (ONAs).' The document's own introduction: 'The current version 2.0 of the ESS QAF was prepared by the ESS Task Force QAF, a sub-group of the Working Group on Quality in Statistics, and Eurostat, and was approved by the European Statistical System Committee in May 2019.'
reports.cadence_note: Two versions on the record, tied to the CoP's own revisions: 'In 2011, when the European Statistics Code of Practice (CoP) was revised for the first time, the European Statistical System Committee (ESSC) adopted the Quality Assurance Framework (QAF) of the European Statistical System (ESS). After the revision of the CoP in 2017, the QAF was substantially enhanced and a revised version was adopted by the ESSC in 2019.' One revision across eight years; 0.13 is that observed interval, not a stated commitment.

reports.title: European Statistical System handbook for quality and metadata reports
reports.description: The ESS's operational guidance for writing quality and metadata reports, and the document that turns SIMS from a structure into a reporting practice. Its own foreword: 'The ESS Handbook for Quality and Metadata Reports (EHQMR) is recognised as an ESS standard. It is included in the Catalogue of ESS standards, the collection of non-legislative normative documents underpinning the ESS.' And: 'This 2020 edition of the ESS Handbook for Quality and Metadata Reports (EHQMR) fully incorporates SIMS 2.0 and the two standards - ESQRS and ESMS - which are unified in SIMS. The document provides guidelines for producer reports and user reports within the overarching SIMS framework.' NOTE: the cover of the same PDF reads '2021 re-edition' while the foreword calls it 'This 2020 edition'; both are quoted and neither is adjudicated.
reports.cadence_note: Editions counted from the Handbook's own lineage statement: 'The first ESS quality guidelines for standard quality reports were adopted in 2003, accompanied by the first ESS Handbook on Quality Reports (EHQR), which was further extended in 2009 to cover all types of statistical processes and incorporate the standard ESS Quality and Performance Indicators.' Three editions - 2003, 2009, and this one - across roughly seventeen years. No stated review interval was found; 0.15 is the observed rate.

reports.title: Single Integrated Metadata Structure (SIMS)
reports.publisher: Eurostat, endorsed by the European Statistical System Committee
reports.description: The ESS's single reporting structure for quality and reference metadata, formed by unifying the two earlier structures. Eurostat's own metadata-standards page: 'SIMS is the inventory and conceptual framework for all ESS quality and reference metadata concepts.' Its live status is stated in the present tense on Eurostat's quality-reporting page: 'The ESS quality reporting standard is the Single Integrated Metadata Structure (SIMS).' The two structures it absorbed remain visible as subsets rather than separate publications: 'the Euro-SDMX metadata structure (ESMS): the ESMS is a subset of SIMS' and 'the ESS standard quality report structure (ESQRS): the ESQRS is a subset of SIMS focusing on detailed quality concepts' - which is why neither is a node here.
reports.cadence_note: Versions, not issues. The EHQMR's lineage statement: 'the two standards - ESQRS and ESMS - were combined in the Single Integrated Metadata Structure (SIMS), which was published in 2013. Minor updates were made in 2015 and SIMS 2.0 was adopted by the European Statistical System Committee.' Eurostat's quality-reporting page additionally lists 'Single Integrated Metadata Structure Guidelines v2.0 (2019)'. Three dated points across 2013-2019; 0.2 is the observed rate, and no stated review interval was found.

reports.title: SDMX Glossary
reports.description: The terminology component of the SDMX Content-Oriented Guidelines, and the published home of the SDMX cross-domain concepts that the ESS's own metadata structure is derived from. The COG's own introduction: 'The SDMX Glossary is an SDMX guideline containing concepts and related definitions that are useful for building and understanding data and metadata exchange arrangements based on SDMX. [...] The Glossary is closely linked to the cross-domain concepts as it also contains all these concepts, stating their definitions and context descriptions.' Maintained by the SDMX Statistical Working Group: 'The development and maintenance of the content-oriented guidelines is under the responsibility of the SDMX Statistical Working Group (SWG), which is made of 20 members from national and international organisations from the statistical and central banking worlds.' The seven SDMX sponsoring institutions are referred to as a group in that document but are nowhere enumerated in the text read, so the publisher field does not enumerate them either.
reports.cadence_note: The weakest cadence in this slice, and stated as such. The Glossary says of itself only that it is updated, with no interval: 'this list will grow and be updated as the SDMX guidelines are used in more and more statistical domains. The Glossary should thus be considered as a "living" document'. sdmx.org names 'The SDMx Glossary Version 2.1 (published in December 2020)'; the same page carries a 'January 2009 version' of the subject-matter domain classification and a February 2016 COG introduction. Roughly one version per decade on the versions observed; 0.1 is that count, not a commitment.

dependencies.basis: Eurostat's Quality Assurance Framework page, 'Aim and content': 'The QAF serves as complementary guidance for how to implement the CoP. Like the CoP, it applies to the statistical authorities of the ESS, which comprises the European Union Statistical Authority (Eurostat), the National Statistical Institutes (NSIs), and Other National Authorities (ONAs). [...] The QAF represents a collection of methods, tools and good practices that are suggested for use or are already in use in some statistical authorities of the ESS. The aim of the QAF is to accompany the CoP by providing guidance and examples in the form of more detailed methods and tools.' Deliberately NOT built on the QAF's own 'follows and aligns with the 2017 revision of the European Statistics Code of Practice' sentence, which is Research.1.md section 5a language; see the caveat entry.

ESS handbook for quality and metadata reports, FOREWORD: 'This 2020 edition of the ESS Handbook for Quality and Metadata Reports (EHQMR) fully incorporates SIMS 2.0 and the two standards - ESQRS and ESMS - which are unified in SIMS. The document provides guidelines for producer reports and user reports within the overarching SIMS framework.'

ESS handbook for quality and metadata reports, FOREWORD: 'The Handbook applies to Eurostat, national statistical institutes and other national authorities in their roles as producers, compilers and disseminators of European statistics. It supports compliance with the European Statistics Code of Practice by providing recommendations on how to prepare comprehensive quality reports for the full range of statistical processes and their outputs.' Recorded as 'cites' rather than 'methodology_depends_on' because the sentence states the Handbook's purpose relative to the CoP rather than a method it takes from it; flagged as a judgement call in _open_questions rather than resolved silently.

Eurostat, Reference metadata reporting standards: 'The 19 high-level concepts are derived from the statistical data and metadata exchange (SDMX) cross-domain concepts published in the SDMX glossary .' The adjacent sentence in the same paragraph - 'The concepts defined in the SIMS standard are compatible with the common terminology established by the SDMX standard' - is Research.1.md section 5a language and carries nothing; the operative clause is 'are derived from'.

The ESGAB annual report's own title page (2021 edition, read in full this session): 'Thirteenth annual report by the European Statistical Governance Advisory Board to the European Parliament and the Council of the European Union on the implementation of the European Statistics Code of Practice by Eurostat and the European Statistical System as a whole'. The Code of Practice supplies the criteria the report is written against.

Eurostat's third-round peer-review page, two statements on the same page. On the exercise: 'Peer reviews form part of the European Statistical System (ESS) strategy to monitor the implementation of the European Statistics Code of Practice (CoP). Their objective is to review the compliance/alignment of the ESS with the CoP and help the statistical authorities to further improve and develop the national statistical systems.' On the report: 'As in previous rounds, Eurostat prepared a final report on the third round of the European Statistical System peer reviews, which has been transmitted to the European Parliament and the Council. This report summarises the results of the peer reviews in all members of the ESS.' This is a two-sentence chain rather than one statement inside the report itself - weaker than the ESGAB edge, and stated as such; SWD(2024) 136 was not opened this session.

_dropped.edge: European Statistics Code of Practice -> Final Report on the ESS Peer Reviews (each CoP revision made on the results of a peer-review round)
_dropped.why: Eurostat's 'History of the CoP' table, verbatim: '24 February 2005 Adoption of the CoP by the Statistical Programme Committee | September 2011 Revision of the CoP based on the results of the 1st round of ESS peer reviews | November 2017 Revision of the CoP based on the results of the 2nd round of ESS peer reviews'. This documents a relationship running the opposite way to the minted ess-peer-review-final-report -> eu-statistics-code-of-practice edge. Not minted, because the quote names 'the results of' a round rather than the titled final report that is the node - the gap between an exercise and its publication, which this corpus does not bridge by inference. Both directions may hold. https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/quality/european-quality-standards/european-statistics-code-of-practice

_dropped.edge: European Statistics Code of Practice -> Regulation (EC) No 223/2009 on European statistics
_dropped.why: The staging records carry Article 11(1) ('The Code of Practice shall aim at ensuring public trust in European statistics by establishing how European statistics are to be developed, produced and disseminated in conformity with the statistical principles as set out in Article 2(1) and best international statistical practice') and Article 11(2) ('The Code of Practice shall be reviewed and updated as necessary by the ESS Committee'), which would support both a Regulation node and this edge. Neither could be re-read at source this session and neither was minted on the inherited quote. EUR-Lex returned HTTP 202 with a zero-byte body to every direct request, and in a real browser every legal-content and ELI form silently redirected to eur-lex.europa.eu/TodayOJ - today's Official Journal - ignoring the CELEX id; publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32009R0223 returned HTTP 400. This is new: the branch's recorded behaviour was that EUR-Lex gates non-browser HTTP but works in a browser. Full URL list in EU/ESSQualityFramework_PartA_2026-08-07.md section G1.

_dropped.edge: Quality Assurance Framework of the ESS -> European Statistics Code of Practice (the 'aligns with' phrasing)
_dropped.why: The QAF's own introduction says: 'The 2019 edition (Version 2.0) of the Quality Assurance Framework of the European Statistical System (ESS QAF) follows and aligns with the 2017 revision of the European Statistics Code of Practice (ES CoP).' 'Follows and aligns with' is squarely in the Research.1.md section 5a family and would not have carried an edge. The minted edge rests instead on Eurostat's 'serves as complementary guidance for how to implement the CoP' / 'aim of the QAF is to accompany the CoP'. Recorded so nobody re-proposes the edge from the weaker sentence, or reads the strong one as resting on it.

_dropped.edge: Quality Assurance Framework of the ESS -> Final Report on the ESS Peer Reviews
_dropped.why: The QAF v2.0 introduction lists its influences: 'It was inspired by the revised ES Code of Practice, Regulation 223/2009 on European Statistics, the two rounds of ESS peer reviews, results and lessons learned from the ESS Vision Implementation Projects, current statistical practices of ESS members as well as other international initiatives and developments'. 'Was inspired by' is not an input claim, and 'the two rounds of ESS peer reviews' names the exercise rather than the report. Searched the QAF for a stronger statement: NOT FOUND (strings searched: 'peer review', 'final report', 'based on').

_dropped.edge: Euro-SDMX Metadata Structure (ESMS) and ESS Standard Quality Report Structure (ESQRS) as nodes
_dropped.why: Both are named repeatedly and neither is minted, deliberately. Eurostat: 'the Euro-SDMX metadata structure (ESMS): the ESMS is a subset of SIMS that focusses on general methodological and quality aspects of the statistical production process' and 'the ESS standard quality report structure (ESQRS): the ESQRS is a subset of SIMS focusing on detailed quality concepts'. The EHQMR says the same from the other side: the two 'are unified in SIMS'. Minting them would double-count against ess-sims - the Report.part_of finding recorded in src/lib/types.ts, and the same call already made for the Eurostat remuneration annexes.

_dropped.edge: ESS Quality and Performance Indicators (2014), ESS Quality Glossary, DESAP checklist as nodes
_dropped.why: All three are named in Eurostat's own 'Tools and standards' list alongside the three documents minted here, and the EHQMR states that the QPIs 'have been incorporated in the Single Integrated Metadata Structure (SIMS)'. Each is one dated publication with no second edition and no stated review interval found, which fails Research.1.md section 4(2). Strings searched on the quality-reporting page and in the EHQMR foreword: 'Quality and Performance Indicators', 'QPI', 'revised', 'edition', '2014'. NOT FOUND.

_dropped.edge: ESS Metadata Handler as a node
_dropped.why: Eurostat: 'the quality of statistical processes and outputs is assessed and reported based on three aspects: standardised rules reporting structures using a common technical environment called the ESS Metadata Handler.' A technical environment, not a publication - closest to a terminus in shape, but it publishes nothing of its own and nothing names it as an input to a report. Logged so it is not rediscovered.

_dropped.edge: SIMS as the Article 12 quality-reporting standard, on the 2015 document's own words
_dropped.why: The 2015 SIMS 2.0 cover says: 'SIMS will be the standard for quality reporting according to Article 12 of Regulation 223/2009 on European statistics.' Future tense in a 2015 document - Research.1.md section 5b running forwards, an announced status rather than a stated one. The present-tense confirmation was found on Eurostat's live quality-reporting page instead ('The ESS quality reporting standard is the Single Integrated Metadata Structure (SIMS)'), which is the route EU/slices/README.md already records: when a methodology document is ambiguous, check whether the release states what it does not.

_dropped.edge: Catalogue of ESS standards as a node class
_dropped.why: The EHQMR describes itself as 'included in the Catalogue of ESS standards, the collection of non-legislative normative documents underpinning the ESS'. A named collection of normative documents is exactly the shape that produces nodes in this corpus, and none of its members other than the three minted here have been looked at. Named, not scoped - a candidate category for the rolling to-do rather than a dropped edge.
